questions.question_text:
A trapezium has parallel sides of $13$ cm and $17$ cm, and the perpendicular distance between them is $8$ cm.
What is its area, in square centimetres?

options.why: Multiplied the height by the sum of the parallel sides but never divided by $2$.

Averaged the two parallel sides but never multiplied by the height.

questions.solution_text:
The parallel sides are the two vertical sides, $11$ cm and $5$ cm, and the $8$ cm side meets both at right angles, so it is the height.
$A=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}$
$=\frac{8(11+5)}{2}$
$=\frac{8 \times 16}{2}$
$=\frac{128}{2}$
$=64\text{ cm}^2$

questions.question_text: Which is the correct formula for calculating the area of a trapezium?

options.why: Halves only one parallel side instead of averaging both.
Divides by height rather than multiplying by perpendicular height.
The standard trapezium-area formula is shown in option A.

questions.solution_text: The area of a trapezium is half the sum of the parallel sides multiplied by the perpendicular height: $A=\dfrac12(a+b)h$.
